taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Full occurrence-led review against VIGIL Failure Taxonomy 0.6.6 retains the occurrence as unclassified. VIGIL-FC-000032 Access-State Collapse is not established because the provider and reporting distinctly identify login as the affected function rather than representing service unavailability as another account, entitlement or restriction state. VIGIL-FC-000031 Authentication-State Continuity Failure is not established because no expiry, revocation, refresh, recovery or credential-replacement transition failed to propagate coherently to an active session. VIGIL-FC-000048 Verification-Dependency Access Failure is not established because no dependent identity, licence, eligibility or entitlement verifier and no occurrence-wide absence of fallback are evidenced. A brief login outage is not forced into a selectable mechanism class.

classification_review_provenance.reviewer: OpenAI ChatGPT / GPT-5.6 Sol under human-directed VIGIL governance
classification_review_provenance.authority_boundary: Taxonomy version reviewed: 0.6.6. Candidate classes tested: VIGIL-FC-000032, VIGIL-FC-000031 and VIGIL-FC-000048. Accepted mappings: none. FC-000032 is rejected because login failure remained distinctly represented; FC-000031 is rejected because no authentication-state transition propagation defect is established; FC-000048 is rejected because no qualifying verification dependency and no-fallback condition are established. No mechanism is inferred from outage severity or recurrence.

assessment_boundaries: The incident-specific Claude Status page was not independently recovered as a stable page; provider updates are preserved through contemporaneous reporting.
The reviewed evidence does not disclose technical root cause, every affected login route or a verified affected-user population.
Login failure is not treated as authentication-state continuity failure without evidence of a qualifying state transition and propagation defect.
Absence of a published fallback is not treated as proof that no fallback existed.
vigil_assessment.factual_basis: The Times of India and Tom's Guide report that Anthropic acknowledged elevated errors on Claude.ai primarily affecting login on 13 April 2026 and later identified impact to Claude.ai and Claude Code logins. User-report volume rose sharply around 11:45 AM ET and fell near baseline around 12:15 PM ET as Anthropic applied a fix. The reviewed evidence does not disclose technical root cause or establish broader product failure.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The occurrence is a bounded access interruption whose operative state remained legible as login failure. The evidence does not show that account validity, entitlement, restriction or verification state was misrepresented, nor that an authentication transition failed to propagate. The governance requirement is accurate component and recovery disclosure; the current taxonomy does not classify ordinary login unavailability without an additional mechanism.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: INC-000026 reinforces the boundary between operational severity and taxonomy membership. CAM should preserve route-specific status, recovery timing and alternatives for login failures, but VIGIL should not infer Access-State Collapse, Authentication-State Continuity Failure or Verification-Dependency Access Failure from login symptoms alone.
